message.content:
The sculpture most frequently cited as the quintessential icon of the 19th‑century art world is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Thinker.”**  
Originally conceived as part of his monumental “Gates of Hell” (1880–1902), the bronze figure was cast in 1902 and quickly became emblematic of modern sculpture, symbolizing introspection, intellectualism, and the human condition. Its widespread reproduction and enduring popularity have cemented it as the most celebrated sculpture of that era.
